archive_anchor.accuracy_note: Described as the REMOTE PRE-RELEASE ARCHIVE ANCHOR, not as absolutely immutable. GitHub's own release object reports immutable=false, and no branch/tag protection rule preventing deletion or movement was observed. The anchor is a real, independently verifiable remote reference; it is not cryptographically or administratively undeletable.

github_release.name: Frozen Main Before Canonical v1 Release.

archive_anchor.peeled_note: not applicable — a lightweight tag has no separate tag object, so the direct SHA IS the commit
archive_anchor.tag_type_evidence: git cat-file -t resolves to 'commit', and ls-remote emits no '^{}' peeled record; an annotated tag would show both

archive_proof.tag_object_sha_note: The requested field assumed an ANNOTATED tag with a distinct tag-object SHA. The tag is LIGHTWEIGHT, so no separate tag object exists: the ref points straight at the commit and rev-parse of the tag and of tag^{} return the same value. This field therefore equals peeled_commit_sha by necessity, not by coincidence, and no tag-object SHA was invented.

manifest_self_hash_method: sha256(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True).encode()) — note NO trailing newline, while the .json file on disk ends with one. RELEASE_MANIFEST.sha256 is written in sha256sum's two-field layout but is NOT verifiable with `sha256sum -c`, because that would digest the file bytes including the trailing newline. Stated explicitly so a future auditor does not read the mismatch as tampering.

merge_into_main.expected_head_precondition: No available tool exposes a server-side expected-head-SHA merge precondition. Enforced instead by re-reading the remote head immediately before the merge and verifying the merge commit's second parent immediately after. Both matched 526e320. This is a weaker guarantee than an atomic precondition and is recorded as such.
